sentences.text: Shunosaurus possessed a very short neck, a feature comparable to members of the family Dicraeosauridae.
Its mouth contained fairly robust but elongated teeth with a crown length reaching up to 8 centimeters.
Because skulls were often compressed or disarticulated, interpretations of the head form have varied from broad and short to extremely narrow and pointed.
The generic name Shunosaurus derives from "Shu", an ancient name for Sichuan.
The specific name honors Li Bing, the governor of Sichuan.
Shunosaurus skeletons are exhibited at the Zigong Dinosaur Museum in Zigong, Sichuan province, and the Tianjin Natural History Museum.
The first Shunosaurus fossil, a partial skeleton, was discovered in 1977 by students excavating a road bank at Dashanpu in Sichuan.
The genus and species Shunosaurus lii were formally described by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, and Zhang Yihong in 1983.
The holotype, IVPP V.9065, was collected from the Lower Xiashaximiao Formation near Dashanpu, Zigong.
The neck length of Shunosaurus indicates it was a low browser.
Researchers suggest Shunosaurus may have used its long thumb claw as a weapon.

Shunosaurus shared its territory with other sauropods like Datousaurus, Omeisaurus, and Protognathosaurus, the possible ornithopod Xiaosaurus, the possible stegosaurian Huayangosaurus, and the theropod Gasosaurus.
Shunosaurus was originally classified as a member of Cetiosaurinae, but in 1992 it was assigned to Shunosaurinae within Cetiosauridae.
Dong assigned it to Shunosaurinae within Cetiosauridae in 1992.
However, a 2002 analysis by Jeffrey Wilson indicated that Shunosaurus had a very basal position within Eusauropoda.
Shunosaurus is classified as a member of the parent group Eusauropoda.
Shunosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
It is debated whether Shunosaurus is related to Rhoetosaurus from Queensland, Australia.
Shunosaurus lived in Sichuan Province, China, during the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) from 161 to 157 million years ago.
Shunosaurus lived from the Aalenian to the Oxfordian stages, between 174.7 and 154.8 million years ago.
Cladistic analyses have produced conflicting results regarding Shunosaurus' classification, with some studies placing it in Euhelopodidae and others indicating a basal position within Eusauropoda.
